blocks.content: Igneous rocks are called primary rocks because they were the first to be formed on the Earth's surface and serve as the parent material for all other rock types.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Igneous rocks are formed through the cooling, solidification, and crystallization of molten magma or lava.
They are classified as primary rocks because all other rock types are directly or indirectly derived from them.
Igneous rocks are crystalline, non-stratified, and completely devoid of organic fossils.
Based on origin, they are divided into intrusive (plutonic) rocks like granite and extrusive (volcanic) rocks like basalt.
Based on chemical composition, high silica content forms acidic rocks (e.g., granite), while low silica and high iron/magnesium form basic rocks (e.g., basalt).

rows: On or near the Earth's surface

items: Igneous rocks do not contain fossils; this is a common trap in competitive exam questions comparing rock types.
The Deccan Plateau of India is predominantly composed of basaltic extrusive igneous rock formed by volcanic fissure eruptions.
Slow cooling deep within the Earth's crust results in large crystalline grains (e.g., Granite), while rapid cooling at the surface produces fine grains (e.g., Basalt).
Key intrusive igneous landforms frequently tested include Batholiths, Laccoliths, Sills, and Dikes.
